views.label: the collapsing cloud
legend: the surface of the cloud, $r = r_b$
the first shell-focusing singularity, at the centre
caption: The Kretschmann scalar $K$ of the inhomogeneous dust cloud over the plane of $t$ and the shell label $r$ ($E = -GM(r)/c^2r$), the same at every $\theta$ and $\phi$. Each shell starts at rest at $R = r$ at $t = 0$ and falls on its own cycloid. The centre reaches $R = 0$ first, at $ct = \pi r_b/\sqrt{5} = 1.4050\,r_b$, the top of the map. The shells $r_b/3$ and $2r_b/3$ collapse at $ct = 1.4543\,r_b$ and $1.6406\,r_b$, and the surface at $ct = \pi r_b/\sqrt{2} = 2.2214\,r_b$.

At release $K = 375/(16r_b^4)$ at the centre and $3/r_b^4$ at the surface. At $ct = 1.3\,r_b$ those values are $3.64 \times 10^{4}/r_b^4$ and $14.286/r_b^4$. Toward the first singularity the central $K$ grows as $80/[27c^4(t_c - t)^4]$, with $ct_c = \pi r_b/\sqrt{5}$. Outside the cloud $K = 12r_s^2/R^6$ with $r_s = r_b/2$, and grows as the freely falling shells shrink.
views.settings: $r_b = 1$, the unit of every length, and $2GM/c^2 = r_b/2$, with $M$ the total mass and $M(r)$ the mass inside the shell labelled $r$.
views.input: Density at release proportional to $1 - r^2/r_b^2$. With $x = r/r_b$, the enclosed mass is $GM(r)/(c^2r_b) = (5x^3 - 3x^5)/8$ inside the cloud and $1/4$ outside it.
views.clip: We colour $K\,r_b^4$ on a logarithmic scale from $10^{-1}$ to $10^6$, over $0 \le r/r_b \le 1.5$ from release to the first central collapse. Values above $10^6$ take the top colour, confined to $r < 0.29\,r_b$ and $ct > 1.36\,r_b$; no cell falls below the lower limit.
